name: Agreement with the Wichita and affiliated bands, October 19, 1872 (never ratified)
aka: Agreement with the Wichita and affiliated tribes, 1872
nations: Wichita and Affiliated Tribes (Wichita, Keechi, Waco and Tawakonie)
Caddo Nation of Oklahoma (Caddo chiefs also signed)
promises: The United States granted the Wichita and affiliated bands, as a home, a tract in Indian Territory between the Washita and main Canadian rivers, from the ninety-eighth meridian west to 98 degrees 40 minutes west longitude.
In return the bands ceded to the United States all claim to lands in Texas, Louisiana, Indian Territory or elsewhere in the United States.

breaches.what: Royce recorded in 1899 that the agreement had never been ratified, although the Wichita had been living on the reserve it described for several years. The Oklahoma State University Kappler edition also tags it not ratified.
breaches.whoFoundIt: Royce, Indian Land Cessions (1899), remarks on area 540A

source.title: Charles C. Royce, Indian Land Cessions in the United States (18th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, 1899), schedule pp. 860-861

breaches.quote: This agreement has never been ratified although the Indians have been in full occupancy of the reserve for several years.

landTaken: None by this agreement, which was never ratified. Royce notes the lands it purported to cede were covered by the claims and earlier cessions of other tribes.
today: The reserve the Wichita occupied was ceded under the agreement of June 4, 1891, ratified by Congress on March 2, 1895 (28 Stat. 876, 897); after the Leased District litigation the Court of Claims entered judgment for the Wichita and affiliated bands of $675,371.91, which was paid. In 1939 the Court of Claims dismissed the Wichita and Caddo claim for aboriginal lands in Oklahoma and Texas (89 Ct. Cl. 378). In Wichita Indian Tribe v. United States, 696 F.2d 1378 (Fed. Cir. January 10, 1983), the court reversed a later dismissal of the Wichita claims (ICC Docket 371, transferred in 1978) and sent them back to the Claims Court to fix the extent of aboriginal title and any liability, expressly taking no view on the nature or date of any taking. The outcome after remand was not traced.

nationVoice.summary: The Tribes' history says that even the reservation established in 1872 between the Washita and Canadian rivers did not remain theirs: led by Tawakoni Jim the Wichita resisted the breaking up of their lands, but in 1900 it was divided into 160-acre allotments with the remainder declared surplus and opened to settlement, which brought the final destruction of the grass house villages and their communal way of life.

The Tribes publish the boundary of the Wichita Reservation, established 1872, between the Washita and main Canadian rivers from the 98th meridian to 98 degrees 40 minutes west, and say it lies today in northern Caddo County and parts of Grady, Canadian, Blaine, Custer and Washita counties.

openQuestions: The Wichita reservation was later allotted and its surplus opened under the 1891 agreement ratified in 1895; that taking belongs to a later record and was not researched here.
The result of the remanded Wichita aboriginal title case (Claims Court, after 1983) was not found; it may hold a finding about the lands this agreement purported to cede.
The Wichita and Affiliated Tribes history pages (wichitatribe.com) did not load for a robot on 2026-11-08, so the nation's own account is missing.
Royce: the reserve overlapped territory assigned to the Cheyenne and Arapaho by the executive order of August 10, 1869.

Audit 2026-11-08: Jordan's rule for unratified treaties checked. No finding was located that the United States took the land of this agreement anyway: the reserve passed under the ratified 1891 agreement (Act of March 2, 1895) with a Court of Claims judgment of $675,371.91 paid (as recited in 89 Ct. Cl. 378), and the courts in 1899 and 1939 held the Wichita had no title to the lands this agreement purported to cede. The 1983 Federal Circuit opinion remands without finding a taking. Status stays unratified. Added the 1939 opinion, the Caddo signatories (OSU text lists Caddo chiefs George Washington, War-Loo-Pee and Antelope) and rewrote today.

Audit 2026-11-08: ICC Docket 257 (Kiowa, Comanche and Apache, with the Wichita as intervenors, 1971) concerns Royce areas 510 and 511 under the 1865 and 1867 treaties, not this agreement; not counted.

plain.promised: The Wichita and allied bands were to get a home between the Washita and Canadian rivers in Indian Territory, and in return give up all claims to land in Texas, Louisiana and elsewhere.
plain.happened: The agreement was never ratified. Royce recorded in 1899 that the Wichita had nonetheless lived on the reserve for several years.
plain.today: The reserve was later given up under a ratified 1891 agreement and the Wichita were paid a court judgment for it. A 1983 appeals ruling revived their claim for older lands; how it ended has not been traced.
